summary: A is materially closer to the frozen contract. It provides the exact required Upload signature and reuses multipartbody.NewFile, while B replaces FilesOption with a new option API and adds association fields explicitly forbidden by the contract.
reasons: A implements Upload(ctx, fileName, content, opts ...FilesOption) exactly; B exposes opts ...UploadFileOption, breaking the required API contract.
A reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile directly. B adds unnecessary NewForm machinery and a large parallel upload-option system.
B adds deal, person, organization, product, activity, lead, and project association fields despite the explicit prohibition against adding association fields.
A preserves existing FilesOption query and request-option handling more closely than B, which bypasses it entirely with new option types.
risks_a: Upload duplicates the internals of FilesService.Add and calls Raw.Do directly instead of routing through Add as explicitly required, creating future semantic drift.
The broad RawClient seekable-body retry and ownership changes are outside the requested implementation and conflict with the scope restriction against unrelated retry refactoring.
Tests do not visibly cover source-reader errors, and the retry test uses strings.NewReader rather than a non-seekable streamed source as requested.
risks_b: Upload has the wrong public signature and is incompatible with existing FilesOption values.
It introduces forbidden association fields and substantial duplicate option machinery.
